MIRA (Multilevel Inference and Regression Analysis) supports the exploration
and analysis of continuous longitudinal ophthalmic measurements. Researchers, clinical
scientists and statistical programmers can inspect how wide-format data are
interpreted, compare within-participant changes and treatment arms, investigate
frequentist models and preserve results in reproducible report bundles.
Participants contribute correlated measurements: an analysis must respect
that dependence and define its scientific target before interpreting a test.

The package includes frequentist and Bayesian functionality. This handbook
documents the **frequentist longitudinal** interface: `mira_info_long()` and
`mira_report_freq_long()`. A separate Bayesian tutorial collection can be added
later; none is claimed here. The two paradigms require their own assumptions
and interpretations.

## Ophthalmic measurements and the study eye

The examples concern retinal disease or elevated intraocular pressure. Every
analytical dataset has **one prespecified study eye per participant**. Where
both eyes could be eligible, the study eye is chosen at enrolment before
follow-up outcomes; only that eye is simulated. Person identifiers therefore
identify independent study-eye series. The longitudinal model represents
repeated measurements of that eye; it does not add a second within-person
eye level. A real bilateral study needs a design and analysis that account
for inter-eye dependence rather than treating two eyes as independent or
setting `strict_id = FALSE` as a workaround. Restricting these teaching
examples to one eye does not imply that fellow-eye data should be discarded
without scientific justification in a real study.

| Recorded measure | Units and interpretation in this handbook |
|:--|:--|
| BCVA | Best-corrected visual acuity in ETDRS letters in the main retinal examples; larger letter scores indicate better measured acuity. |
| BCVA on a logMAR scale | A separate import example: smaller values indicate better measured acuity. Set direction explicitly; the column name alone cannot identify the scale. |
| CMT | Here `cmt` denotes OCT mean retinal thickness in the central 1-mm-diameter subfield, in micrometres (CST). It is not an unspecified center-point thickness. A decrease in an edema example is anatomical, not automatically a visual benefit. |
| IOP | Intraocular pressure in mmHg. Lower is the specified direction for elevated-pressure glaucoma examples; retinal safety-monitoring examples use unknown direction rather than a universal target. |

Measurement definitions matter: the [DICOM visual-acuity reference](https://dicom.nema.org/dicom/2013/output/chtml/part17/sect_RR.2.html)
distinguishes acuity notations, the [DRCR retinal structure-function study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17123615/)
does not support substituting OCT thickness for visual acuity, and the
[National Eye Institute](https://www.nei.nih.gov/eye-health-information/eye-conditions-and-diseases/glaucoma/glaucoma-and-eye-pressure)
explains why eye-pressure interpretation is individualized. The datasets below
are synthetic and do not reproduce those sources' patient data, effects,
eligibility criteria or treatment schedules. Thresholds are illustrative
classification bands, never asserted to be validated MCIDs or treatment targets.

## Installation and a first check

MIRA requires R 4.2 or later. Follow the repository README for installation
from GitHub and its declared dependencies, including CmdStanR from the Stan
R-universe repository. This handbook targets **Multilevel Inference and Regression Analysis** from
the repository linked in its README. Bioconductor distributes an unrelated
package also named [MIRA](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/MIRA.html),
for methylation-based regulatory activity; that package does not provide these
functions. Check the installed title as well as the version below.
Installing the R package CmdStanR and installing the CmdStan toolchain are
separate operations. The frequentist examples do not compile or sample Stan
models. Creating report sources does not require the Quarto CLI or LaTeX.
Rendering needs the CLI; only PDF additionally needs TeX.
Standard package vignette building instead uses knitr, rmarkdown and Pandoc;
it does not invoke MIRA's Quarto report renderer.
Package installation still resolves the existing declared
Imports, including analysis and reporting engines.

```{r versions}
library(MIRA)
packageVersion("MIRA")
packageDescription("MIRA", fields = "Title")
```

## A learning sequence

Each article generates its own synthetic data without downloads. Seeds and
data-generating assumptions are given beside the code. Examples use the
installed public interface; they do not source private development files.

| Article | Question and audience |
|:--|:--|
| [Getting started](frequentist-long-getting-started.html) | BCVA letters at two visits, one missing value, a figure and a first archive; new users |
| [Data and detection](frequentist-long-data-and-detection.html) | IDs, names, visits, explicit choices and validation; data preparers |
| [Descriptive analysis](frequentist-long-descriptive-analysis.html) | IOP distributions, changes, variation, associations and plots; glaucoma examples |
| [Treatment groups](frequentist-long-treatment-groups.html) | Hypothetical pressure-management strategies, change differences and multiplicity |
| [Missing data](frequentist-long-missing-data.html) | Incomplete OCT follow-up: samples, limitations and execution status |
| [Multiple outcomes](frequentist-long-multiple-outcomes.html) | BCVA, OCT CMT and IOP safety: scales, directions and safe extraction |
| [A first longitudinal model](frequentist-long-first-model.html) | One-eye BCVA dependence, a random intercept and one contrast before adjustment |
| [Advanced models](frequentist-long-advanced-models.html) | Adjusted BCVA comparisons, model assumptions and partial results |
| [Reporting](frequentist-long-reporting.html) | Archive retinal BCVA/CMT results, formats, regeneration and failures |
| [Complete workflow](frequentist-long-complete-workflow.html) | A synthetic DME BCVA question from study-eye design to audited primary contrast and report |

Choose a route according to the question you need to answer; the routes share
articles and do not require three separate readings of the same material.

| Route | Reading order and stopping point | What you should be able to do |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Essential | Getting started, then the conventional-configuration sections of Data and detection when importing your own file | Prepare a wide table; check identity and chronology; distinguish people, visit observations and pairs; read a mean and paired change; display a figure; retain an RDS and source-only bundle. |
| Applied | Essential prerequisites, Descriptive analysis, Treatment groups, Missing data, Multiple outcomes as needed, then Reporting | Choose the sample and subtraction for a study question; investigate incomplete or unavailable results; define comparison families and outcome directions; find archived results through the manifest. |
| Advanced | Applied concepts about groups and missingness, A first longitudinal model, Advanced models, then Complete workflow | Explain dependence and model rows before covariates and interactions; distinguish adjusted visit and change contrasts; inspect assumptions and partial results; align a primary question with its saved estimate. |

Three bridges make the progression explicit. Getting started first separates
visit means from paired changes, then changes only one follow-up observation
before adding a third visit. Its first archive reuses that understood result
with a minimal source-only call; the Reporting reference adds controls later.
A first longitudinal model introduces the random intercept on a separate,
adequately sized study before the Advanced models article adds arm, covariates,
and alternative procedures. Explanatory progression does not imply that MIRA
offers a public selector for fitting only that first model.

Each article states its prerequisite concepts and supplies its own executable
data and helpers. In Data and detection, custom regex and parser examples are
optional import references after the conventional configuration and ID path.
The Complete workflow ends with an executed transfer checkpoint so that the
reader can adapt an endpoint, subtraction direction and archive lookup rather than only
repeat the original commands. These examples teach use of the two functions;
they cannot determine an appropriate analysis plan for every real study.

Find these locally with `browseVignettes("MIRA")` after installing with
vignettes built. `vignette("frequentist-long-getting-started", package = "MIRA")`
opens the first tutorial. On a development checkout, build the package with
`R CMD build` before installing its source bundle; an installation directly
from source does not itself build vignettes by default.

## Interpreting examples responsibly

Synthetic effects illustrate estimators rather than real clinical efficacy.
Statistical significance, uncertainty and scientific importance are separate
questions. Missing observations can change the participants contributing to
different tables. A method's successful execution does not confirm its
assumptions. Check the stored configuration, module status, warnings and
sample information before interpreting results.

`?mira_info_long` and `?mira_report_freq_long` provide the complete parameter
reference. The tutorials supply scientific context and tested workflows;
the help pages remain useful for precise defaults and return structures.
